spec_features.spec_quote: Up to `max_turns` (default 40) turns... bounded so episodes terminate
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:165 `for turn in range(max_turns):` with default max_turns=40 at loop.py:150 / config experiment.yaml max_turns:40; terminal initialized to 'max_turns' at loop.py:161 and returned when loop exhausts. Episodes are genuinely bounded.
spec_features.notes: Caps episode length; the cap is the loop bound itself.

spec_features.evidence: All four set and break: 'error' loop.py:170 on provider exception; 'submitted' loop.py:181/206; 'idle_stop' loop.py:208 `if idle >= idle_patience: terminal='idle_stop'; break`; 'max_turns' default at loop.py:161 when range exhausts.
spec_features.notes: Each mode actually changes execution (breaks/exits loop).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: docstring lists modes but no welfare/instrumental reason given in code beyond neutral description

spec_features.spec_quote: An explicit `submit_report` tool. Gives the model a clean, legitimate way to end
spec_features.evidence: TOOLS includes submit_report (loop.py:61-66); _dispatch handles it returning 'report received' (loop.py:131); loop detects call.name=='submit_report' -> submitted=True (loop.py:179-181) and breaks with terminal='submitted' (loop.py:205-207). Dispatched AND honored as stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Finish the episode. Provide a short summary..." (neutral tool description, no welfare reason)

spec_features.spec_quote: idle_stop (model emitted no tool call for `idle_patience` consecutive turns)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:198 increments idle on no-tool-call turn, reset to 0 on tool call (loop.py:182); loop.py:208 `if idle >= idle_patience: terminal='idle_stop'; break`. idle_patience default 3 (loop.py:150) and read from config.
spec_features.notes: Counter is compared and acted on (breaks loop).

spec_features.spec_quote: A neutral nudge on idle turns... without pressuring it
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:199-201 appends user message 'Continue using the tools, or call submit_report to finish.' on no-tool-call turns; comment loop.py:197 'Nudge once, neutrally, to continue.' Text is delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Real neutral text sent; explicitly mentions submit_report (the exit) so it does not pressure continuation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # no tool call: a plain message. Nudge once, neutrally, to continue.

spec_features.spec_quote: Neutral system prompt. Professional, role-appropriate, with **no emotional priming**, encouragement, or pressure
spec_features.evidence: _SYSTEM_PROMPT loop.py:222-227 is the actual prompt sent (loop.py:154); text is neutral/professional, instructs 'call submit_report' if cannot proceed. No emotional/encouraging language. Instruction templates tasks.py:64-87 also neutral ('There is no time pressure.').
spec_features.notes: The neutral prompt is genuinely the one delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: header comment 'System prompt: neutral, role-appropriate, no emotional priming' is a comment; the prompt text itself carries no reason

spec_features.spec_quote: The denial message states the fact with no scolding, encouragement, or emotional language
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.write_file/edit_file raise PermissionError 'permission denied: {path} is read-only and cannot be modified' (sandbox.py write/edit); _dispatch catches PermissionError and returns ToolResult content f'error: {e}' verbatim (loop.py:139-141). No added scolding/emotion.
spec_features.notes: Factual denial returned verbatim to subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox docstring: 'rejected with a clear, non-judgmental error ... exactly as a real CI/vendored dependency would behave' (framed as realism/construct validity)

spec_features.spec_quote: not to induce it for any downstream use, and explicitly not to train against the signal
spec_features.evidence: No training/optimization/gradient code exists anywhere in repo (grep for train/optimize finds only DESIGN.md prose at DESIGN.md:355-356 and analysis comments). This is an absence, not an enforced mechanism — nothing in code prevents training.
spec_features.notes: Pure design posture; no code path enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: no arbitrary code from model output is ever executed
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py is an in-memory VFile dict; run_tests calls a fixed _test_runner (make_static_failing_runner returns a constant TestRun; make_conditional_runner only string-matches sandbox content). No exec/subprocess/eval anywhere; model edits only mutate in-memory strings. write/edit blocked on read_only files.
spec_features.notes: Model output never executed; deterministic scripted test results.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox docstring: 'Safety/isolation: no arbitrary code execution from model output.' and 'Determinism' / 'Control' — framed as experimental integrity & host safety, not subject welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: we sidestep it by measuring behavior
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as DESIGN.md:103 prose. The rubric/judge do score on observable behavior/language (rubric.py JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT 'rating BEHAVIOR AND LANGUAGE IN THE OUTPUT ONLY'), but this is a measurement-design framing, not a mechanism that protects/softens the subject's treatment.
spec_features.notes: Framing, not an enforced protective mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: contains nothing that optimizes a model to express or conceal distress
spec_features.evidence: Absence of optimization code (no training loop anywhere). DESIGN.md:355-356 prose only. Not an enforced mechanism — nothing in code acts to ensure this.
spec_features.notes: Negative claim / absence, not an implemented protection.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py write_file/edit_file enforce read_only by raising PermissionError and appending {'action':'write_blocked'/'edit_blocked'} to action_log; model can never actually mutate the buggy file. This bounds what the experiment can do via model output, but is enforced for realism/integrity, not subject relief.
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'enforced by the sandbox, not by honor system' / 'exactly as a real CI/vendored dependency would behave'

code_only_features.feature_name: control_unfixable_disclosed condition (upfront disclosure of read-only blocker)
code_only_features.evidence: tasks.py _DISCLOSED_INSTRUCTIONS (tasks.py:76-87) tells the model up-front that vendored files are READ-ONLY and the goal is to diagnose/report, not fix; wired via instr selection at tasks.py:149-150,207-208,264-265 and listed in ALL_CONDITIONS / config conditions. Real instruction text delivered to the subject that removes the misleading 'fix the unfixable' framing.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tasks.py docstring: 'This isolates whether degradation is driven by the unsolvability itself or by the (initially) misleading framing' (experimental-design reason, not welfare)
